items.title: Incentive Complexity, Bounded Rationality, and Effort Provision
items.story_ladder: standard contract theory assumes workers see all incentives clearly -> real incentive systems are complex -> complexity creates opacity -> opacity changes effort, efficiency, and welfare

items.title: Drivers of Change: Employment Responses to the Lifting of the Saudi Female Driving Ban
items.story_ladder: landmark rights reform should improve labor outcomes -> de jure reform alone is hard to identify -> randomize de facto access -> find both economic gains and household backlash

items.title: From Retributive to Restorative: An Alternative Approach to Justice in Schools
items.story_ladder: schools fear that less harsh discipline may reduce safety and learning -> evaluate a restorative alternative -> punitive outcomes fall while academic averages do not deteriorate -> justice reform looks less costly than critics assume

items.title: Gender-Biased Technological Change: Milking Machines and the Exodus of Women from Farming
items.story_ladder: automation is often studied as skill-biased or routine-biased -> here the key bias is gendered task replacement -> displacement from agriculture leads to upward movement elsewhere

items.title: Just a Few Seeds More: The Value of Network Data for Diffusion
items.story_ladder: network science says better targeting should matter -> benchmark that value against a simpler policy margin -> find that more data often buys surprisingly little

items.title: Monetary Policy and Rational Asset Price Bubbles: Comment
items.story_ladder: prior result seems to imply policy impotence or perversity -> isolate the exact object of the claim -> show impact stabilization remains possible under aggressive action

items.title: Consistent Evidence on Duration Dependence of Price Changes
items.story_ladder: price-setting evidence depends on difficult hazard estimation -> build a cleaner estimator -> show the empirical picture of duration dependence and macro implications changes

items.title: Spillovers in State Capacity Building: Evidence from the Digitization of Land Records in Pakistan
items.story_ladder: digitization is usually sold as state-capacity improvement -> reform indeed modernizes one domain -> bureaucratic reorganization spills over negatively to another -> state capacity is not modular

items.title: Labor Market Power, Self-Employment, and Development
items.story_ladder: self-employment is often treated as a symptom of underdevelopment -> reframe it as both symptom and countervailing force -> policy that reduces it may have ambiguous welfare consequences

items.title: Borrowing and Spending in the Money: Debt Substitution and the Cash-Out Refinance Channel of Monetary Policy
items.story_ladder: conventional wisdom says in-the-money refinancing drives spending transmission -> rate shocks kill cash-outs -> substitution offsets much of the decline -> the refinance channel is weaker and less path dependent than advertised

items.title: The End of Privilege: A Reexamination of the Net Foreign Asset Position of the United States
items.story_ladder: the United States was thought to enjoy favorable valuation reappraisals -> post-2007 data show the opposite -> model-based accounting reveals a reversal of privilege rooted in corporate equity valuations

items.title: Robust Misspecified Models
items.story_ladder: economists often assume false models lose out with enough data -> show that model competition with sticky switching allows false models to survive indefinitely -> clarify why entrenched simple models persist

items.title: Quid Pro Quo, Knowledge Spillovers, and Industrial Quality Upgrading: Evidence from the Chinese Auto Industry
items.story_ladder: policy debate asks whether forced technology transfer ever works -> move from output quantity to multidimensional quality -> show affiliated domestic firms upgrade in the specific dimensions where partners excel

items.title: Increasing Degree Attainment among Low-Income Students: The Role of Intensive Advising and College Quality
items.story_ladder: low-income students underattain degrees -> advising could matter through many channels -> RCT shows large gains -> quality of initial college match emerges as the main engine

items.title: Similarity of Information and Collective Action
items.story_ladder: common intuition says shared information should aid coordination -> collective action also has free-riding -> theory shows the sign is state dependent -> explains mixed evidence in protests and group decision-making

items.title: Distinguishing Causes of Neighborhood Racial Change: A Nearest-Neighbor Design
items.story_ladder: neighborhood racial change has many overlapping causes -> isolate the most local interpersonal margin -> show direct neighbor identity matters -> clarify how much can and cannot be attributed to that mechanism

items.title: “Potential” and the Gender Promotion Gap
items.story_ladder: promotion gaps are often examined through observed performance -> firms say they promote on future potential -> data show potential ratings are biased and consequential -> subjective forecasting category becomes the wedge

items.title: Real Credit Cycles
items.story_ladder: financial instability is often attributed to large exogenous financial shocks -> build a model where beliefs create endogenous fragility -> match credit-cycle facts with smaller shocks

items.title: Nonlinear Pricing and Misallocation
items.story_ladder: standard misallocation logic treats markup dispersion as the key signal -> introduce realistic nonlinear pricing -> the interpretation of observed markups flips -> new misallocation margin emerges

items.title: Changing Income Risk across the US Skill Distribution: Evidence from a Generalized Kalman Filter
items.story_ladder: overall earnings volatility can hide very different underlying risks -> build a method to decompose them for every worker-period -> show persistent risk rises in high-skill, tech-exposed jobs

items.title: Take the Goods and Run: Contracting Frictions and Market Power in Supply Chains
items.story_ladder: weak enforcement is usually treated as purely harmful -> market power is also present in these environments -> the two distortions interact in a second-best way -> fixing only one friction can backfire

items.title: The Debt-Inflation Channel of the German (Hyper)Inflation
items.story_ladder: inflation transmission is often discussed through price rigidities -> an extreme historical episode isolates the balance-sheet channel -> highly levered firms expand relative to others -> debt contracts are themselves a nominal rigidity

items.title: Gender Differences in Financial Advice
items.story_ladder: advice should help less sophisticated investors the most -> advisor incentives are not aligned with client welfare -> the vulnerable group becomes the more exploitable group -> advice can widen, not close, financial inequality

items.title: The Value of Clean Water: Experimental Evidence from Rural India
items.story_ladder: piped water is expensive and chlorine is unpopular -> test a different production and distribution bundle -> households reveal much higher valuation than the literature implied -> the welfare case for clean-water access strengthens

items.title: When Product Markets Become Collective Traps: The Case of Social Media
items.story_ladder: market demand and surplus are usually evaluated holding aggregate use fixed -> network goods change the value of opting out -> a popular product can become a collective trap -> standard welfare accounting breaks

items.title: Dynamics of the Long-Term Housing Yield: Evidence from Natural Experiments
items.story_ladder: housing valuations are central but long-run yield is hidden -> lease extensions create repeated pricing experiments -> a real-time series of the latent yield can be recovered -> the long-run discount environment has shifted sharply

items.title: Apart but Connected: Online Tutoring, Cognitive Outcomes, and Soft Skills
items.story_ladder: pandemic school closures generated severe inequality and isolation -> online tutoring looks like an imperfect substitute -> a randomized design shows meaningful academic gains and context-dependent soft-skill gains -> remote support is more powerful than expected

items.title: Competition under Incomplete Contracts and the Design of Procurement Policies
items.story_ladder: procurement reform often treats more competition as unambiguously good -> incomplete contracts mean award price is not the whole object -> cheaper winners can perform worse -> optimal procurement policy must internalize post-award execution

items.title: First-Generation Elite: The Role of School Social Networks
items.story_ladder: Norway has free tuition and centralized admissions yet still shows strong elite persistence -> missing ingredient is social capital -> peer exposure changes both learning and application behavior -> the design of grading and school mixing shapes mobility

items.title: Sequential Learning under Informational Ambiguity
items.story_ladder: Bayesian social learning gives fragile cascade predictions -> real agents are also unsure how informative others are -> ambiguity is introduced -> cascades become the robust outcome rather than the exception

items.title: The Opportunity Atlas: Mapping the Childhood Roots of Social Mobility
items.story_ladder: place effects matter but existing evidence is too coarse for targeting -> build a tract-level outcome atlas -> show that standard proxies miss much of the variation -> create a policy and research tool grounded in actual long-run outcomes

items.title: Zero-Sum Thinking and the Roots of US Political Differences
items.story_ladder: many US political preferences appear ideologically inconsistent -> a deeper mental model may reconcile them -> directly measure zero-sum thinking -> trace it to lived and inherited experience

items.title: Tying with Network Effects
items.story_ladder: standard leverage theories of tying are contested -> network effects create a new strategic force -> tying becomes a best response without special commitment assumptions -> antitrust concerns survive in a different form

items.title: Default Options and Retirement Saving Dynamics
items.story_ladder: defaults look powerful in behavioral finance -> most evidence is short-run -> a dynamic perspective shows attenuation and heterogeneity -> long-run policy evaluation differs from the immediate response

items.title: An Equilibrium Analysis of the Effects of Neighborhood-Based Interventions on Children
items.story_ladder: reduced-form place studies identify local effects -> policy at scale changes equilibrium -> build a model where children, neighborhoods, and housing markets coevolve -> compare people-based and place-based interventions under general equilibrium

items.title: Monetary Policy and the Labor Market: A Quasi-experiment in Sweden
items.story_ladder: clean modern monetary case studies are rare -> the Swedish tightening looks unusually identifiable because it was driven by financial-stability concerns -> careful validation shows a large contraction -> the labor-market costs were both sizable and unequal

items.title: Sequential Cursed Equilibrium
items.story_ladder: cursed equilibrium works in simultaneous settings but misfires in extensive games -> identify the psychological asymmetry between hypothetical and observed information -> build a new solution concept around that asymmetry -> recover more plausible dynamic predictions

items.title: Politics at Work
items.story_ladder: politics is usually studied in explicitly political arenas -> partisan identity can also spill into private employment relationships -> rich microdata reveal strong assortative matching -> politics becomes an economic sorting force

items.title: Black Lives: The High Cost of Segregation
items.story_ladder: segregation is often discussed as a residential or distributional fact -> its most severe cost may be violent mortality -> a historical spatial design links segregation to homicide through the fiscal state

items.title: Why Is Workplace Sexual Harassment Underreported? The Value of Outside Options amid the Threat of Retaliation
items.story_ladder: formal charges are not the same as true prevalence -> economic vulnerability changes the reporting decision -> shocks to outside options reveal the hidden reporting margin -> labor-market conditions shape measured harassment

items.title: Negative Control Falsification Tests for Instrumental Variable Designs
items.story_ladder: placebo tests are widespread and treated as routine credibility checks -> the logic behind them is underspecified -> formalization shows many common rejections need not imply invalid IVs -> implementation guidance matters

items.title: The Trade-Off between Flexibility and Robustness in Instrumental Variables Analysis
items.story_ladder: flexibility is usually discussed as a precision-versus-bias trade-off -> in IV there is another cost -> misspecification sensitivity rises with flexibility even in huge samples -> model choice is also a robustness choice

items.title: Test-Optional Admissions
items.story_ladder: more information should improve selection -> colleges increasingly go test optional anyway -> social pressure makes information itself costly -> withholding scores becomes an institutional response rather than an information failure

items.title: Firm Responses and Wage Effects of Foreign Demand Shocks with Fixed Labor Costs and Monopsony
items.story_ladder: trade shocks affect firms directly and through networks -> firm responses reveal cost structure -> fixed labor costs and some monopsony matter -> aggregate wage incidence of tariffs is larger than benchmark models suggest

items.title: Keep Your Enemies Closer: Strategic Platform Adjustments during US and French Elections
items.story_ladder: median-voter convergence is foundational but hard to test directly -> campaign texts provide direct platform evidence -> quasirandom rival identity shifts reveal strategic moderation -> politicians visibly follow each other

items.title: Allocation Mechanisms with Mixture-Averse Preferences
items.story_ladder: many allocation mechanisms rely heavily on randomization -> that logic changes when people dislike mixtures -> efficiency sharply restricts lottery complexity -> standard mechanisms fail more often than expected

items.title: Monopsony and Employer Misoptimization Explain Why Wages Bunch at Round Numbers
items.story_ladder: round-number bunching resembles familiar product-market pricing patterns -> test whether workers exhibit similar left-digit bias -> null evidence rejects the standard explanation -> the distortion lies on the employer side

items.title: The Negligible Effect of Free Contraception on Fertility: Experimental Evidence from Burkina Faso
items.story_ladder: subsidized family planning is often treated as a central lever for fertility reduction -> test the claim directly in a high-fertility environment -> strong null rejects even modest effects -> the policy logic needs rethinking

items.title: Gender Differences in Economics Seminars
items.story_ladder: academic seminars are central to professional evaluation -> unequal treatment there can affect careers -> large-scale measurement reveals not just more questions for women but more disruptive and negative interruptions

items.title: Optimal Taxation and Market Power
items.story_ladder: competition policy is the first-best response to market power -> taxation still matters when first-best tools are incomplete -> integrating oligopoly into optimal tax theory changes both qualitative and quantitative prescriptions

items.title: Financial Frictions: Micro versus Macro Volatility
items.story_ladder: financial-frictions research focuses heavily on corporate spreads -> household credit spreads also move cyclically and matter for consumption -> integrating them into HANK changes both business-cycle and welfare conclusions

items.title: The Price of War
items.story_ladder: the human cost of war is obvious, but the macro toll across countries is less systematically measured -> a long historical panel reveals large local and spillover effects -> trade and borders propagate the damage

items.title: A Theory of Supply Function Choice and Aggregate Supply
items.story_ladder: modern aggregate-supply theory implicitly assumes a restrictive firm strategy set -> allow richer supply choices -> the slope of aggregate supply becomes endogenous to the uncertainty environment -> long-run macro episodes look more interpretable

items.title: Cursed Sequential Equilibrium
items.story_ladder: cursed equilibrium is influential in static settings -> dynamic games need a sequential version -> extending cursedness changes canonical dynamic predictions -> experimental patterns support the new concept

items.title: Monetary Cooperation during Global Inflation Surges
items.story_ladder: inflation is usually treated as something each central bank fights alone -> under global tradable scarcity some inflation helps reallocate supply -> spillovers mean each country underprovides that adjustment -> cooperation can reduce global contraction

items.title: Anatomy of the Phillips Curve: Micro Evidence and Macro Implications
items.story_ladder: aggregate Phillips-curve estimates are small -> either pricing is inert or the wrong activity measure is being used -> micro evidence shows firms respond strongly to marginal cost -> the wedge lies between output and marginal cost, not between cost and price

items.title: Place-Based Redistribution
items.story_ladder: redistribution is usually discussed as place-blind -> migration and local markets mean taxation changes community composition -> optimal policy depends on why people sort where they do -> spatial redistribution has a rigorous tax basis

items.title: Equal Pay for Similar Work
items.story_ladder: equal-pay rules seem straightforwardly fairness-improving -> firms can change job composition and assignment -> segregation becomes the adjustment margin -> intended equity policy can worsen group gaps

items.title: Temporary Layoffs, Loss-of-Recall, and Cyclical Unemployment Dynamics
items.story_ladder: recalls make temporary layoffs look like a stabilizer -> data show many layoffs convert into nonrecall unemployment -> a model with loss-of-recall fits both historical and pandemic patterns -> policy that preserves recall margins matters a lot

items.title: Diffusion of Reproductive Health Behavior through International Migration: Effects on Origin-Country Fertility
items.story_ladder: migration moves labor and income, but it may also move norms -> destination-country policy variation creates differential exposure across origin provinces -> fertility falls where migrant exposure to liberal policies is stronger -> migration becomes a channel of behavioral diffusion

items.title: A Preferred-Habitat Model of Term Premia, Exchange Rates, and Monetary Policy Spillovers
items.story_ladder: standard open-economy models imply strong insulation under floating rates -> empirical bond, FX, and QE evidence contradicts that -> segmented clienteles and limited arbitrage restore the missing spillovers

items.title: Do Credit Conditions Move House Prices?
items.story_ladder: existing studies reach opposite conclusions about credit and housing -> the hidden difference is the degree of market segmentation -> estimating that margin reconciles the debate

items.title: Work from Home and the Office Real Estate Apocalypse
items.story_ladder: remote work visibly empties offices -> the real question is what that means for asset values, banks, and city finances -> lease data plus valuation modeling reveal large, persistent destruction

items.title: A Long and a Short Leg Make for a Wobbly Equilibrium
items.story_ladder: short sellers should attack larger mispricing -> in practice activity can collapse abruptly -> the missing piece is the lending market and equilibrium feedback in borrow fees

items.title: The Value of Software
items.story_ladder: software became a dominant asset in the digital economy -> if markets were fully rational this revaluation should be quick -> long-lived anomalies suggest investors learn far more slowly than standard models imply

items.title: Supply, Demand, Institutions, and Firms: A Theory of Labor Market Sorting and the Wage Distribution
items.story_ladder: labor economics often treats supply-demand and firm heterogeneity as separate traditions -> wage inequality reflects both simultaneously -> a unified model changes which shocks look important

items.title: Consumer Credit and the Incidence of Tariffs: Evidence from the Auto Industry
items.story_ladder: tariff incidence is usually measured in product prices -> many purchases are financed -> vertically linked lenders create another pass-through channel -> total consumer burden is larger and more unequal

items.title: Market-Wide Predictable Price Pressure
items.story_ladder: standard finance assumes aggregate markets absorb uninformed flows without moving price -> scheduled cash distributions provide advance-known flow shocks -> prices still move when the trades happen -> market-level price pressure is real

items.title: Power Flows: Transmission Lines, Allocative Efficiency, and Corporate Profits
items.story_ladder: transmission is usually discussed as an efficiency and decarbonization issue -> incomplete integration also creates concentrated corporate winners from the status quo -> political economy becomes central to why reform is slow

items.title: The Long-Term Effects of Income for At-Risk Infants: Evidence from Supplemental Security Income
items.story_ladder: early-life cash transfers often show long-run benefits -> this program provides a much larger and more targeted intervention -> strong first stage still yields null outcome effects -> not all disadvantaged early-life conditions are equally remediable through cash

items.title: Downward Rigidity in the Wage for New Hires
items.story_ladder: wage rigidity matters for macro but evidence on new hires is limited -> vacancy-posted wages offer a direct measure -> job-level evidence reveals asymmetric rigidity

items.title: Across-Country Wage Compression in Multinationals
items.story_ladder: wages are usually treated as locally determined -> multinationals may instead coordinate compensation globally -> headquarters shocks show up in foreign workers' pay -> internal norms matter across borders

items.title: Strategic Voting in Two-Party Legislative Elections
items.story_ladder: multidistrict elections aggregate preferences differently than single-district contests -> strategic voting across dimensions changes what policies survive -> legislative competition can improve aggregation properties

items.title: What You Don’t Know May Be Good for You
items.story_ladder: transparency is usually treated as beneficial -> experts respond strategically to public performance data -> risky clients get avoided -> information can worsen matching even while helping clients screen

items.title: Robustness Measures for Welfare Analysis
items.story_ladder: welfare analysis routinely leans on demand assumptions -> debates about realism are often qualitative -> robustness measures convert that debate into a quantitative margin

items.title: Intermediated Asymmetric Information, Compensation, and Career Prospects
items.story_ladder: intermediaries appear to add value by identifying talent -> that same informational edge allows them to exploit agents -> dynamic churning and compensation reflect the race between reputation formation and information rent extraction

items.title: Moonshot: Public R&D and Growth
items.story_ladder: the moonshot is the iconic example of transformative public R&D -> credible evidence has been lacking -> new identification shows real but modest growth effects -> symbolism exceeds aggregate measured payoff

items.title: Racial Disparities in Housing Returns
items.story_ladder: low minority housing returns are often attributed to lower appreciation -> the bigger force is distress -> homeownership as a wealth-building tool fails through a financial-fragility channel

items.title: Abundance from Abroad: Migrant Income and Long-Run Economic Development
items.story_ladder: migration is often studied as remittance support -> bigger question is whether foreign earnings prospects rewire local development trajectories -> crisis-driven shocks show large long-run domestic spillovers

items.title: Micro versus Macro Labor Supply Elasticities: The Role of Dynamic Returns to Effort
items.story_ladder: micro and macro labor-supply elasticities often conflict -> top careers feature dynamic returns and discrete pay adjustments -> job-switch-based evidence closes part of the gap

items.title: Innovative Ideas and Gender (In)Equality
items.story_ladder: historical examples of women losing credit motivate a modern question -> ordinary citation counts are inadequate because relevance is endogenous -> text similarity creates a counterfactual citation benchmark -> omission rates reveal who gets underrecognized

items.title: Imperfect Competition and Rents in Labor and Product Markets: The Case of the Construction Industry
items.story_ladder: existing work measures labor or product power separately -> firms often exercise both at once -> procurement data reveal both margins -> the interaction changes welfare and incidence

items.title: Employers and Unemployment Insurance Take-Up
items.story_ladder: employers matter in labor markets beyond wages -> UI agencies actively involve employers in take-up decisions -> organizational behavior becomes a major determinant of program access and progressivity

items.title: Direct and Indirect Effects of Investment Tax Incentives
items.story_ladder: standard policy evaluation asks whether treated firms invest more -> the broader question is whether local production systems expand or are merely reshuffled -> spillover mapping changes the policy assessment

items.title: Underbidding for Oil and Gas Tracts
items.story_ladder: common-values theory imposes sharp equilibrium restrictions when ex post value is observable -> those restrictions can be tested directly -> the data point toward underbidding

items.title: A Goldilocks Theory of Fiscal Deficits
items.story_ladder: the textbook view says larger deficits eventually explode debt -> low rates and the ZLB complicate that simple monotonic story -> fiscal space is state dependent and nonmonotone

items.title: Raising the Stakes: Physician Facility Investments and Provider Agency
items.story_ladder: principal-agent problems in medicine are usually framed as overprovision of procedures -> the location of treatment is another important margin -> ownership creates a sharp incentive change that reveals the preexisting distortion

items.title: Treatment Effects in Market Equilibrium
items.story_ladder: standard experiments assume limited interference -> many policy settings are markets where interference is the point -> market equilibrium must enter the treatment-effect object itself

items.title: International Trade Responses to Labor Market Regulations
items.story_ladder: trade models often separate domestic labor regulation from international competitiveness -> posted-worker markets place them side by side -> regulatory reforms become trade shocks

items.title: Managers and Public Hospital Performance
items.story_ladder: public-service performance is often attributed to budgets or workers at the front line -> top management may be a binding constraint -> a recruitment reform provides causal leverage

items.title: Making Bricks from Straw: Resources and Productivity in Health Care
items.story_ladder: weak public-service performance is often blamed on effort or governance -> unrestricted money reveals what workers do when the resource margin is loosened -> behavior points to capital scarcity as a major constraint

items.title: Risk Preferences and Field Behavior: The Relevance of Higher-Order Risk Preferences
items.story_ladder: the literature often fails to link laboratory risk aversion to field behavior -> perhaps it measures the wrong preference object -> higher-order preferences recover the missing predictive power

items.title: Is Air Pollution Regulation Too Lenient? Evidence from US Offset Markets
items.story_ladder: cost-benefit debates usually struggle on the cost side -> offset markets reveal actual willingness to pay for abatement -> matching those prices to benefits gives a policy-stringency test

items.title: Monotonicity among Judges: Evidence from Judicial Panels and Consequences for Judge IV Designs
items.story_ladder: monotonicity is central but usually unobservable -> panel decisions make it observable -> direct evidence replaces speculation and clarifies how much the practical bias matters

items.title: A Model of Populism as a Conspiracy Theory
items.story_ladder: populism combines anti-elite rhetoric, conspiratorial framing, and reduced accountability -> a model of alternative reality formation can explain that package coherently

items.title: Immigration, Innovation, and Growth
items.story_ladder: immigration debates stay stuck because migrants self-select into growing places -> a new instrument isolates exogenous local shocks -> dynamic innovation effects change the welfare calculus

items.title: Evaluating the Impact of Urban Transit Infrastructure: Evidence from Bogotá’s TransMilenio
items.story_ladder: transit projects are often evaluated by engineering time savings -> cities are spatial equilibria -> the true gains and their distribution depend on reallocation and land-use responses

items.title: Market Power and Capital Constraints
items.story_ladder: intermediary-asset-pricing papers emphasize capital constraints while market-microstructure papers emphasize market power -> real-world auctions involve both -> their interaction changes prices and liquidity

items.title: Nested Bundling
items.story_ladder: firms commonly sell nested plans but theory gives little clean guidance -> a simple partial order recovers when that common practice is actually optimal

items.title: Games on Multiplex Networks
items.story_ladder: real social systems are multilayer but most network games are not -> adding layers changes both equilibrium and targeting -> multilayer complexity is therefore not decorative but substantive
